title: Cache TLB saturation and paging investigation (wip)
body:
Purpose and context
- Short: root-cause investigation for intermittent token-latency spikes correlated with high KV cache activity. We're exploring whether TLB pressure and page-level paging behavior (hugepage usage, allocation stride, read patterns) are amplifying memory bandwidth and eviction costs.

Observed symptoms (production & repro)
- Production traces: tail token latency spikes (99th percentile) on large-sequence chat sessions (avg seq > 2k tokens).
- Spike signature: CPU-side scheduling is stable; GPU utilization steady, but host-side pre- and post-processing latency (KV cache lookup phase) shows ~1.5–3x increase on affected requests.
- Repro environment: microbench harness that replays KV access patterns extracted from traces reproduces increased latency when sequence lengths produce deep KV reuse and high interleaving of different sessions.

Hypotheses (ranked)
1) TLB saturation: KV store's many small allocations cause excessive dTLB misses and page walks under heavy working-set churn.
2) Page fragmentation & small-page pressure: allocator returns many 4KB pages, leading to more page table entries than necessary; hugepages (2MB) could reduce page-table pressure.
3) Associativity conflicts in CPU caches due to allocation stride/power-of-two buckets causing increased eviction of critical KV metadata in L1/L2/LLC.
4) DRAM bandwidth hotspots due to poor prefetching for random KV accesses, magnified by repeated page walks.

Profiling artifacts and commands used (repro VM, pinned CPU cores)
- perf record -a -g -F 2000 -e cycles,instructions,cache-references,cache-misses,LLC-load-misses,dtlb-load-misses,dtlb-store-misses -o perf.data -- ./kv_repro --workload traces/session_replay.json
- perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > perf.folded; flamegraph.pl perf.folded > flame.svg
- Intel PCM counters via pcm-memory for DRAM bandwidth samples.
- pmap /proc/<pid>/map and pagemap reads to inspect large page mappings and residency.
- custom allocator tracing: KV_ALLOCTRACE=1 logs allocation size, alignment, page count.

Key measurements (representative)
- Baseline (no hugepages): dTLB-load-misses ~ 1.2M/min, page-walks ~ 85k/min, LLC-load-misses 320k/min, host KV lookup P50=1.8ms, P99=14.2ms.
- With experimental 2MB hugepages pinned: dTLB-load-misses reduced ~72%, page-walks reduced ~66%, LLC-load-misses down ~28%, KV lookup P50=1.7ms, P99=8.9ms.
- DRAM bandwidth: baseline 420 GB/s peak on host node during repro; with hugepages down to 310 GB/s peak (pattern smoothing).
- Eviction counts (measured via KV eviction counter): baseline eviction churn increased during spikes by ~2.3x relative to steady state; with hugepages, eviction churn only ~1.4x.

Interpretation notes
- Hugepages materially reduced TLB misses and page-walk overhead; that alone explains most of the P99 latency improvement. This suggests page-table pressure was a dominant factor.
- The LLC and DRAM bandwidth reductions imply that fewer page walks correlate with fewer random DRAM reads (page walks touch memory regions for page tables).
- Residual tail after hugepages is likely due to allocation stride leading to cache set conflicts (associativity) in L1/L2/LLC for the KV metadata and pointer arrays.

Micro-experiments and results (short log)
- Experiment A: switch allocator to 2MB-aligned arenas + madvise(HUGEPAGE) at startup. Result: P99 down from 14.2ms to 9.1ms. TLB misses down 70%.
- Experiment B: scatter/gather re-layout of KV bucket headers (padding to 64B) to reduce alignment clashes. Result: LLC-load-miss delta -9%, tail latency -~6% further.
- Experiment C: change jemalloc config to background-thread purge disabled (reduce churn). Result: small improvement on P50, no significant P99 change.
- Experiment D: enable software prefetch for sequential KV scans with a threshold. Result: DRAM BW smoothing but only marginal tail improvement.

Open questions and follow-ups
- Is hugepage allocation safe on Dedicated nodes where multiple GPU tenants run? Need to measure memory isolation and OOM behaviors under mixed workloads.
- Eviction policy interaction: does reducing TLB/page pressure change eviction ordering? (We saw slight change in hotset residency).
- Can we adopt a hybrid approach: large pages for metadata/indexing, small pages for dense payloads? How to enforce from the runtime/allocator?
- Are there any kernel-level knob regressions (kernel version differences) that explain why some fleets see strong effect and others less? Need kernel matrix testing.

Proposed mitigation plan (short-term -> mid-term)
- Short-term (sprint): enable optional hugepage mode behind a config flag and runtime switch; add health gating in node-init to refuse hugepage mode if memory low. Add telemetry for dTLB misses, page-walks to console dashboards (Optimize/Console).
- Mid-term: implement KV allocator arenas that prefer large pages for metadata and maintain size-class awareness to avoid associativity conflicts. Add randomized offset/padding for bucket arrays to mitigate cache-set collisions discovered in associativity tests.
- Long-term: explore a software-managed TLB-friendly slab allocator and a per-model working-set placement strategy that reduces cross-session interference. Consider OS/kernel collaboration (transparent hugepages vs explicit hugetlbfs).

Experiment plan (next 6 runs)
- Run matrix across 3 kernel versions (5.10, 5.15, 6.0), 2 allocator configs (jemalloc default, hugepage arenas), 3 workload mixes (small convo, long convo, mixed). Collect perf counters, flamegraphs, pagemap snapshots.
- Safety check: stress test OOM scenarios with hugepages enabled (simulate memory fragmentation).
- Telemetry: add a lightweight host-side probe to report per-node dTLB misses and page-walks per minute to Influx; correlate with P99s.

Notes for PR and rollout (links)
- PR that implements hugepage arena + config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1793 (draft, needs fuzzer + canary).
- Jira task for rollout gating and metrics: INF-4821. See Confluence doc for design: confluence:serving-runtime/kv-tlb-investigation.

Appendix: quick repro steps for team
1) checkout branch kv-hugepage-arena from serving-runtime.
2) provision repro VM with 64GB host RAM, enable hugetlbfs: mount -t hugetlbfs none /mnt/huge -o pagesize=2M.
3) build: make -C ./serving-runtime build-repro
4) run: ./build/kv_repro --config repro/config-long-seq.json --hugepage-dir /mnt/huge --pin-cpus 2-7
5) capture: perf record -o perf.data -e cycles,dtlb_load_misses,DTLB_LOAD_MISSES ./build/kv_repro
6) compare p99 numbers in logs and collect perf report.

Immediate action items (who/when)
- Priya: add dTLB/page-walk metrics to Console and create dashboard tile (next 5 working days).
- Jin: extend canary test to optionally enable hugepages and run on 5 instances in us-west-2 (end of week).
- Liam: run kernel-compatibility matrix on small fleet and report regressions (next 10 days).

Notes-to-self
- This doc is a working log — keep raw perf artifacts in /mnt/kv-profiling/artifacts/<date>. Zip the flamegraphs and attach to INF-4821.
- Follow up: evaluate the effect on Dedicated nodes where evictions are more expensive due to pinned capacity.

End of notes
